item.text: {"question_id":"5B.6","answer":"In 2023, Tshisekedi’s government made and partly implemented a substantial public-investment agenda, but the supplied record does not establish consistently timely, high-quality, or nationally distributed results. Tshisekedi directly prioritized investment in health, education, rural development, and national infrastructure in the 2023 budget guidance (BATCH-0023-E013). The presidentially organized PDL-145T had launched 313 school and health-centre works in 48 territories, with additional contracts covering 731 infrastructures and projected deliveries during 2023 (BATCH-0023-E001); by August, the government reported more than 300–400 works ready, against planned schools, health centres, and administrative buildings (BATCH-0019-E009). These reports demonstrate implementation activity, but remain executive claims and do not verify final quality, completion, service use, or equitable distribution. World Bank-supported governance and education operations supported treasury, procurement, digital revenue systems, telecommunications, utilities, and girls’ education, while the government’s free-primary-education policy was associated with 3.6 million additional enrolled pupils in 2021–2022; however, these were partner-supported or earlier-period measures and do not establish exclusive presidential causation or learning quality (BATCH-0014-E003; BATCH-0014-E004). Execution and capacity were materially uneven: the 2023 accounts review cited budget overruns, uncertified debts, and works listed without observed field action (BATCH-0024-E004); a government dissolution of the Social Fund paused disbursements for three World Bank-financed projects during transition (BATCH-0017-E002); and a WFP-led resilience programme fully implemented only half of planned activities, with weak coordination (BATCH-0002-E001; BATCH-0002-E004). Independent conditions also remained severe: more than 2,000 schools closed amid insecurity and displacement, nearly 7 million children were out of school, and healthcare infrastructure in the east was fragile (BATCH-0022-E010; BATCH-0008-E002). FAO and WFP further reported that conflict disrupted infrastructure and agriculture and that insufficient rural investment impeded food self-sufficiency, though they did not attribute these conditions specifically to Tshisekedi (BATCH-0022-E013). Overall, the evidence supports real budgetary and implementation effort with some reported outputs, but not a finding that executed resources reliably produced high-quality, timely public goods rather than incomplete, weakly verified, or partner-dependent projects.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0023-E013","BATCH-0023-E001","BATCH-0019-E009","BATCH-0014-E003","BATCH-0014-E004"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0024-E004","BATCH-0017-E002","BATCH-0002-E001","BATCH-0002-E004","BATCH-0022-E010","BATCH-0008-E002","BATCH-0022-E013"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The supplied evidence does not independently verify PDL-145T completion, construction quality, timeliness, service use, procurement integrity, or nationwide distribution.","Several positive outputs and programmes involved executive agencies, the World Bank, WFP, UNICEF, FAO, or other partners; exclusive attribution to Tshisekedi is not established.","Some adverse outcomes reflect conflict, displacement, structural capacity limits, or humanitarian funding shortages, so they cannot be assigned entirely to presidential decisions.","The evidence is stronger for budget priorities, programme activity, and reported outputs than for technology, administrative-capacity outcomes, predictable regulation, or durable service quality."],"corrections_made":["Removed the unsupported implication that reported construction, free education, and partner projects themselves establish productive, high-quality public investment.","Added the Social Fund dissolution and paused disbursements, ineffective enforcement and shortages, school closures and exclusion, and insufficient rural investment/infrastructure disruption.","Distinguished presidential attribution from government, partner, agency, conflict, and structural responsibility.","Separated priorities and planned or reported implementation from independently verified outcomes and quality."] ,"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":["Independent audits and completion records for PDL-145T and other 2023 capital projects could materially clarify timeliness, quality, distribution, and patronage risk.","Executed budget-by-sector data and service-use or learning-quality indicators are needed to test whether appropriations translated into durable public goods.","Evidence on subsequent correction of budget irregularities, Social Fund transition outcomes, and rural infrastructure delivery remains incomplete."]}
